Keep the phase-specific response unknown.

state_response.summary: The Kathmandu Post reports batons and water cannon during the march. Arrest accounts are phase-ambiguous: the Jan. 26 follow-up quotes a police spokesperson denying arrests at the march, while NHRC’s official statement refers broadly to arrest during a Jan. 25 protest without separating the nearby rights-defender gathering.

end_date.summary: The opened reports describe water-cannon dispersal but do not establish when participants physically departed or when the gathering ended; the end date remains unknown.

notes: The Kathmandu Post reports actual use of batons and a water cannon during the Jan. 25 march. Its Jan. 26 follow-up quotes a police spokesperson denying arrests during this civil-society march. The NHRC’s official Jan. 26 statement broadly refers to police arrests during a Jan. 25 protest but does not separate this march from the earlier rights-defender gathering, so the march-specific arrest code remains unknown. It separately reports a rights-defender gathering whose participants were detained; that separate gathering is recorded as E013. Injury accounts conflict: police reported five protesters and five security personnel injured and treated, while campaigners said more than a dozen protesters were injured and six remained hospitalized. No crowd count or physical ending is established. A prohibited-zone entry does not establish protester violence.
